title: TikTok Shop Taxes: The Complete 2026 Guide for Sellers
summary: How TikTok Shop sellers handle taxes in 2026: 1099-K rules, sales tax, write-offs, quarterly payments, and a step-by-step filing guide.
body_markdown:
## Key takeaways


-


**TikTok Shop income is taxable** whether or not you receive a 1099-K.


-


For 2025 onward, TikTok Shop issues a **Form 1099-K** once you pass **$20,000 in sales and 200 transactions,** but several states set their thresholds far lower (as little as $600), so be sure to check state-specific requirements.


-


You'll owe **income tax plus 15.3% self-employment tax** on your profit, so a good rule of thumb is to set aside **25–30%** of what you earn.


-


**TikTok collects and remits sales tax for you** in most states (because of its role as a "marketplace facilitator"), so most sellers don't file sales tax on TikTok Shop sales.


## Are you a TikTok Shop seller or an affiliate?


-


**Sellers:** you list and sell your own products. This guide is for you.


-


**Affiliates / creators:** you earn commissions promoting other people's products, and often receive free samples. Your forms and write-offs are different, so read our guide to[TikTok Shop affiliate taxes](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/tiktok-affiliate-taxes) instead.


If you sell on TikTok Shop, the money you make is taxable income. Let's break it down.


## Do you have to pay taxes on TikTok Shop income?


Yes. If you make money on TikTok Shop, it's all taxable income. The IRS treats money you earn selling products as self-employment income.


-


**I didn't get a 1099-K. Do I still owe taxes?** The 1099-K is just a report of your payments. Whether or not you get one, you're still legally required to report the income you earned. So if you didn't get a 1099-K, you'll have to reconstruct how much you earned and pay taxes on it!


-


**What if I'm doing TikTok Shop as a hobby?** If you're selling with the intent to make a profit, the IRS considers it a business, and business income is taxable. Hobby income is also taxable, but hobbies can't deduct expenses. If you need help differentiating between a "hobby" and "business", check out Keeper's[guide](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/business-vs-hobby) .


-


**What about affiliate commissions and free samples?** Those are taxable too, but they work differently from sales. See our[TikTok Shop affiliate tax guide](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/tiktok-affiliate-taxes) .


> **Keeper pro tip:** The moment TikTok Shop stops being "fun money" and starts being income you'd miss, treat it like a business. Open a separate[bank account](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/how-to-open-a-business-bank-account) and start[tracking expenses](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/track-1099-expenses) . Deducting your business expenses is the single biggest lever you have to lower your taxable income.

### The 2026 1099-K threshold


For the 2025 tax year onward, the federal 1099-K threshold is **more than $20,000 in gross sales AND more than 200 transactions.** However, there are 2 big caveats to this threshold:


1.


**Some states require a 1099-K at much lower amounts.** States like Maryland, Massachusetts, Vermont, Virginia, and Illinois have thresholds as low as $600–$1,000. If you live in one, you should expect to get a 1099-K!


2.


**You still owe taxes even if you didn't meet the threshold or didn't get a 1099-K.** Even though the threshold is $20,000 and 200 transactions, if you made $8,000 and never get a 1099-K, that $8,000 is still taxable!


### Your 1099-K won't match your payouts, and here's why


Most people realize the number on their 1099-K is almost always higher than the cash that actually hits their bank account.


That's because the 1099-K reports **Unadjusted Gross Sales (UGS)** - product price plus shipping fees, minus only your discounts. It excludes refunds, TikTok's platform fees, commissions, shipping subsidies, and timing differences.


Practically, that means if you simply report the 1099-K number as your income, you'll overstate your revenue and overpay in taxes.


> **Keeper pro tip:** Make sure to pull your **1099-K detailed report** (or Orders/Settlement report) from Seller Center and reconcile it before filing!


### Why did TikTok withhold 24% of my payments?


When you set up TikTok Shop, you're asked to provide tax info (a **W-9** with your SSN or EIN). If you don't, TikTok is required to withhold 24% of your payments (what's called a "backup withholding"), and you may lose the ability to sell. 😱 To add your tax info, go to **Account Settings → Tax** .


## Does TikTok Shop collect and remit sales tax?


Yes, in almost all states, TikTok Shop automatically collects and remits sales tax on your behalf.


Under state "marketplace facilitator" laws, the platform (not the individual seller) is responsible for collecting and paying sales tax on sales made through it. That covers all 45 states (plus DC) that levy sales tax.


As a seller, that means:


-


You generally **don't need to collect or file sales tax** on your TikTok Shop sales.


-


But you may still have obligations if you sell on other channels (your own store, in person), or if you have physical nexus (e.g., inventory stored in a state).


### Why is TikTok Shop charging higher sales tax?


Sales tax is destination-based. It's calculated on your buyer's location, and many areas stack state, county, and city rates. So the rate varies order to order!


> **Keeper pro tip:** Sales tax and income tax are totally separate. TikTok remitting sales tax does nothing for your income tax. You still owe income plus[self-employment tax](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/what-is-self-employment-tax) on your profit.


## How much tax will I owe from TikTok Shop sales?


You owe two things on your profit (income minus expenses):


1.


[Self-employment (SE) tax](https://www.keepertax.com/1099-tax-calculator) **: 15.3%** (12.4% Social Security plus 2.9% Medicare). This is on top of income tax and catches most first-timers off guard.


2.


[Income tax](https://www.keepertax.com/income-tax-calculator) **:** at your marginal rate, which depends on your total household income.


Let's see an example: Maria sells phone accessories on TikTok Shop and nets **$30,000 in profit** in 2026.

That's why the rule of thumb is to set aside **25–30% of your profit** for taxes. (Use[Keeper's free 1099 tax calculator](https://www.keepertax.com/1099-tax-calculator) to plug in your own numbers.)


**Quarterly estimated taxes:** If you expect to owe **$1,000 or more** for the year, the IRS expects you to pay in four quarterly installments throughout the year. If you miss them, you could end up owing an underpayment penalty![Here's how quarterly taxes work.](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/how-to-file-quarterly-taxes)

## What can you write off on TikTok Shop?


If you sell on TikTok Shop, you can write off "ordinary and necessary" business expenses to lower your taxable income. Common tax write-offs for[online sellers](https://www.keepertax.com/tax-write-offs/online-seller) include:


Category


Examples


**💰 Cost of goods sold (COGS)**


What you paid for the inventory you sold


**💸 TikTok fees**


Platform commission, transaction/affiliate fees, TikTok Ads spend


**📦 Shipping & packaging**


Postage, boxes, mailers, labels, tape


**🎁 Product samples**


Items you buy to demo or create content with


**🎥 Content gear**


Ring light, phone/camera, tripod, mic, backdrops, props


**💻 Software & subscriptions**


Design tools, bookkeeping apps, scheduling tools


**🏡 Home office**


A portion of rent/utilities if you have a dedicated workspace


**📱 Phone & internet**


The business-use percentage


**🚗 Mileage**


Trips to the post office, suppliers, pop-ups


**🧾 Professional fees**


Accountant, tax software, business license


> **Keeper pro tip:** The write-offs people miss most are[home office](https://www.keepertax.com/home-office-deduction) , the business-use percentage of their[phone bill](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/how-to-deduct-cell-phone-bill-on-taxes) , and[mileage](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/freelancers-guide-to-writing-off-car-expenses) !

## What about free samples and affiliate commissions?


If you also promote other sellers' products as an affiliate, your commissions are self-employment income and any free samples you keep count as income at their fair market value. Affiliates are paid on a different form than sellers, so we cover the details, including how to offset sample income with write-offs, in our[TikTok Shop affiliate tax guide](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/tiktok-affiliate-taxes) .


## How to file your TikTok Shop taxes: step by step


1.


**Get your tax documents ready.** Your 1099-K (Seller Center → Finances → Tax) and your 1099-K detailed / Settlement report for reconciliation.


2.


**Total your real gross income.** Start from UGS, then reconcile out refunds and fees to get your true revenue.


3.


**Add up your**[deductions](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/what-is-a-tax-deduction) **.** If you haven't been tracking them consistently, get an app like[Keeper](https://keeper.tax/file-taxes) , which links to your accounts and cards to automatically track and categorize your business expenses.


4.


**Fill out**[Schedule C](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/schedule-c) (Profit or Loss From Business). Revenue minus expenses = your net profit.


5.


[Calculate self-employment tax](https://www.keepertax.com/1099-tax-calculator) **on Schedule SE** (15.3% of net profit).


6.


**Report it on your Form 1040** , along with any W-2 or other income.


7.


[Pay quarterly taxes](https://www.keepertax.com/quarterly-tax-calculator) if you expect to owe $1,000 or more.


## Tax tips for TikTok sellers, from a CPA


-


**Reconcile the**[1099-K](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/what-is-form-1099-k) **.** The UGS figure is likely inflated, so make sure to file off your actual revenue.


-


**Treat inventory correctly.** Most small sellers can deduct inventory as "non-incidental materials and supplies" rather than tracking complex inventory accounting. This is often simpler and better.


-


**Consider separating business banking.** A dedicated account can make bookkeeping easier on you.


-


**Consider an S-Corp.** Once your profit is consistently high (roughly $60K-$80K or more), an[S-corp election](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/what-is-an-s-corp-and-should-i-start-one) can reduce your self-employment tax. (See how much an S-Corp could save you in taxes with Keeper's[free S-Corp tax savings calculator](https://www.keepertax.com/s-corp-savings-calculator) .)


-


**Watch out-of-state inventory nexus.** If a fulfillment service stores your inventory in other states, you may create sales tax nexus there even though TikTok collects and remits sales tax on your behalf.


-


**Don't forget the**[QBI deduction](https://www.keepertax.com/posts/qbi-deduction) **.** Many self-employed sellers qualify to deduct an extra 20% of qualified business income.

*TikTok Shop taxes come down to one idea: it's self-employment income, so you owe income plus self-employment tax on your profit, but every business expense lowers that profit.
